summary: Iteration 24 testing — Backend home_copy behavior PASS (15/15 tests including regression). Frontend admin nav restructure PASS (4 primary tabs, sub-toggles, Leads slide-over all render correctly). SkeletonGrid on /works and /gallery PASS. Admin gallery pagers (top+bottom) + admin Lightbox with prev/next/close/counter/img testids PASS. CRITICAL frontend bug: AdminSEOManager save() sends an empty PUT body → 422 → toast tries to render error object array → app-wide React crash (ErrorBoundary 'Something needed a quiet reset'). Home Copy save, Footer save, Nav save — all SEO edits appear broken via the UI. Real-time sync tests could not be verified because save fails.

ui_bugs.issue: save() uses `let latest; setDoc((cur)=>{latest=cur; return cur;}); await api.put('/admin/seo', latest);` — in React 18 the functional-updater may not run before the subsequent api.put call, so `latest` is undefined at send time, resulting in PUT /api/admin/seo body=null. Backend returns 422 with FastAPI detail array. The catch block then calls `toast.error(e?.response?.data?.detail || 'Save failed.')` — passing an ARRAY of error objects to sonner Toast → React throws 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {type, loc, msg, input, url})' → ErrorBoundary crashes the entire admin app to the 'Something needed a quiet reset' screen. Reproduced 100% on every SEO Save click (Home Copy line1 change, etc.).

toast.error() must receive a string. Coerce array/object errors: `typeof detail === 'string' ? detail : JSON.stringify(detail)`. Without this fix, ANY backend 422 anywhere in this flow will crash the admin app.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot verify polling-based real-time sync because the underlying save is broken (see AdminSEOManager bug). action_items: URGENT: Fix AdminSEOManager.save() — replace the `let latest; setDoc((cur)=>{latest=cur;...})` pattern with a plain `latest = doc` (state is stable at click time) or use a ref. Also coerce toast.error payload to string: `const msg = typeof (e?.response?.data?.detail) === 'string' ? e.response.data.detail : (e?.message || 'Save failed.'); toast.error(msg);`

After fix, re-verify: (a) Home Copy save publishes to `/api/seo` (b) Public / hero updates within 20-25s poll cycle without hard reload (c) Clearing home-copy-hero-line1 + save falls back to compiled 'Redefining' default (d) Existing SEO/Footer/Nav saves still work.

Spec listed them without the prefix — treat as spec typo, code is consistent.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminSEOManager.jsx save(): the 'sync via functional setState' pattern is unreliable — the updater is scheduled but not guaranteed to run before the following async call. Use `doc` directly (setState value at handler invocation time is what the current render captured) or a `useRef` mirror. This is the root cause of the admin app crash.

AdminSEOManager error handling must never pass raw response.data.detail (which FastAPI returns as an ARRAY of error objects) to a React-rendered toast/text node. Always stringify or extract the .msg field.

AdminDashboardPage.jsx: sub-tab testid naming is consistent (`admin-subtab-{primary}-{sub}`). The review request lists shorter selectors for hero-covers; recommend either updating the spec or aliasing testids for backward compat.
Backend home_copy sanitizer (_sane_visible + only-truthy-string mutation) works exactly as designed — empty/whitespace inputs never overwrite defaults, verified by pytest.

rca of the issue: Root cause: AdminSEOManager.jsx save() line 108-123. Pattern `let latest; setDoc((cur)=>{latest=cur; return cur;}); await api.put('/admin/seo', latest);` — the updater callback runs during React's state reconciliation, which under React 18 auto-batching may occur AFTER the synchronous continuation of the async function (the api.put invocation). Result: `latest` is `undefined` at PUT time → axios sends empty/null body → FastAPI Pydantic validation returns 422 with `[{type:'missing', loc:['body'], input: null, ...}]` → error handler does `toast.error(e.response.data.detail)` where detail is an ARRAY of error objects → sonner renders it as a React child → React throws 'Objects are not valid as a React child' → the app-level ErrorBoundary catches → shows 'Something needed a quiet reset' page. Fix: use `doc` directly (React state closes over the value; there's no rapid-edit-before-click race worth this hack) OR mirror doc into a ref. Additionally, sanitize the toast payload to always be a string.
